The ratings map for Kuehne + Nagel International
Every answer the Investment Analyst wrote in the four layers behind this memo, word for word
The Financial Analyst Memo: every financial table and model output behind this memo

Kuehne + Nagel International (KNIN-CH): a better-run forwarder at a top-quintile multiple, facing a two-year earnings plateau that consensus has not modelled

Prepared 9-Nov-26 for Richard. The share price is CHF 236.7 (29-Oct-26), the 52-week high; the 52-week low is CHF 143.85. The Financial Analyst's model, whose forecasts this memo uses, was run at CHF 227.10 on 26-Oct-26, and each return quoted from today's price says so. The fiscal year ends in December. The next results, with the first FY2027 guidance, are due on 2-Mar-27. Amounts are in CHF millions unless stated; the definitions of EBIT, gross profit, free cash flow, EPS and consensus are in the end notes.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in five sentences. Kuehne + Nagel is a genuinely better-run business than it was in 2024. Its 2026 recovery was well executed, but the forces that drove it were mostly temporary and external. The shares trade at a top-quintile multiple just as earnings enter a two-year plateau that consensus has not yet modelled. From March 2027, after a last round of beats, estimate revisions are skewed to the downside. The real opportunity is the trough-on-trough setup that the stock is likely to offer in 2028.

The ten things that matter.

supports the sharesweighs on the sharesthe forecast itself
  1. Kuehne + Nagel's 2026 recovery is real. Recurring EBIT rises from CHF 1,380m to about 1,554m (+13%) and conversion from 14.1% to 17.1%. Guidance was raised three times, lifting the midpoint by about 20%. In Q3 2026 Sea volumes grew 4.5% and Air volumes 10% against a market growing 2% to 4%, and Sea operating cost per twenty-foot equivalent unit (TEU, the standard container measure) fell 8.5%. Management has done what it said it would do.
  2. The forces that delivered the 2026 recovery are the most temporary ones available. DSV's integration of Schenker handed over road, air and sea share; Red Sea and Hormuz disruption held ocean yields up; tariff front-loading and US restocking lifted volumes; and a semiconductor and hyperscaler boom drove Air EBIT up 84% in Q3. Each of these forces has a dated end inside 2027.
  3. One external variable, Sea and Air unit gross profit, rules the forecast. Sea and Air produce about 42% of gross profit but about 78% of EBIT, because their costs move with volume rather than with price. Each 1% on Sea and Air gross profit per unit is therefore worth about CHF 38m of EBIT (2.4%, or CHF 0.24 of EPS). Three forces push that variable down: container fleet growth of 9.5% in 2027 and 12.7% in 2028 against demand growth of about 4%, Suez transits already back at 58% to 59% of 2023 levels (75% is the trigger for falling yields), and returning air capacity.
  4. The base case is an earnings plateau, not a continuation of the recovery. Viewforth's recurring EBIT stays between CHF 1.50bn and 1.59bn from FY2026 to FY2029 and reaches 1,721m only in FY2030, while EPS dips from CHF 9.30 to 8.86 in FY2028. Viewforth's EBIT is 8% below consensus for FY2027, 13% for FY2028 and 17% for FY2029, and about 70% of that gap is Sea and Air unit gross profit.
  5. Self-help sets a floor under earnings; it does not grow them. The CHF 200m cost programme and the CHF 100m to 150m artificial-intelligence (AI) target are gross figures. Wage inflation of about CHF 130m a year, volume-driven hiring (headcount +9%) and savings passed on to customers absorb most of them, so operating costs still rise 1.2% to 1.4% a year. The savings are why EBIT is flat instead of down 10% to 15%.
  6. Guidance and fundamentals will diverge in 2027. Kuehne + Nagel sets a low annual range in March and then raises it. Expect a FY2027 range centred on CHF 1.5bn to 1.55bn (below consensus) on 2-Mar-27, beats and probably a raise in April and July, the first miss in October 2027 against the CHF 435m Q3 2026 base, and a flat FY2028 range in March 2028. A raise in 2027 does not disprove the plateau; the FY2028 range is the test.
  7. Consensus sits near Viewforth's bull case. Three-quarters of Viewforth's FY2027 distribution lies below consensus EBIT of CHF 1,644m. Expect estimates to be cut in two steps, in March 2027 and October 2027, with a pause between them. Only 17% of analysts rate the shares a Buy, and the median target (CHF 219.5) is 7% below the price: analysts have raised their numbers but not their recommendations, the signature of a mature upgrade cycle.
  8. The share price has decoupled from its sector and is driven by company news at the top of its range. The shares are up 54% in twelve months, at the 91st percentile of relative strength, and only 21% of their six-month movement is explained by the logistics basket. The two-year-forward P/E is about 22x on consensus EPS (83rd percentile of ten years) and about 25x on Viewforth's EPS, while DSV sits at the 2nd percentile of its own history. The multiple is supported by the beat-and-raise cycle, which ends in H2 2027.
  9. The return at the guideline fair multiple is thin and depends on the recovery years. At 22.93x two-year-forward EPS (the guideline for the Broadening phase), total return from CHF 227.10 is +5.1% to 31-Mar-28 (3.6% a year) and +16.9% to 30-Sep-29 (5.5% a year); from today's CHF 236.7 each is about four points lower. The earnings part of that return (+7.1% and +16.5%) comes from FY2029 and FY2030 entering the valuation window, the least certain years in the forecast. From today's price the bull case returns about +20% and the bear case about -35%, so the probability-weighted return is roughly zero with a wide range of outcomes skewed to the downside.
  10. Cash is the hedge, and the dividend is safe. Falling freight rates release working capital, so free cash flow rises to about CHF 1.35bn in 2027 while EBIT falls. Free cash flow covers the 80% payout (CHF 7.50, 7.25 and 7.00 a share) about one and a half times, and the Foundation that owns the majority may smooth it. There is no solvency or dividend risk in this case; the risk lies entirely in earnings expectations and the multiple.

Five judgements move the value most (the arithmetic is in #6): the level of Sea and Air unit gross profit after the 2027 contract season; how much of the gross savings reaches EBIT after inflation, hiring and pass-through to customers; how much of the 2026 volume share survives DSV's recapture and a possible pause in technology air demand; the franc; and the multiple the market will pay once the guidance raises stop.

What would make me wrong, positively. Three signals would point to the bull case: Sea gross profit per TEU holding above about CHF 440 through Q2 2027 while Suez transits stall below 75% of 2023 levels and port congestion keeps absorbing new ships; constant-currency operating cost growth below 2% with volumes growing 4%; and a FY2027 range set near consensus in March. If any two of the three appear, the bull case (FY2027 EBIT about CHF 1.68bn, EPS about CHF 10) becomes the base case, and the shares can hold their multiple into 2028.

#1 Operating environment: tailwinds and headwinds

Conclusion: the strong 2026 tailwind is turning into a scheduled headwind, so the net external picture over the next 12 to 24 months is mildly negative, and its timing is unusually knowable.

Evidence: the tailwinds. Six external forces lifted 2026, and almost all of them end inside 2027. A simple test sorts them by durability. "Use" forces reflect real demand or share and last longest; "refill" forces, such as restocking, last a few quarters; "price" forces, such as surcharges and diversions, reverse when their cause goes. Customs complexity is the only force with no dated end, and it is the smallest.

Evidence: the headwinds are scheduled, not speculative.
  • Ship supply. Container deliveries of about 3.1m TEU in 2027 and 4.4m in 2028 come from an orderbook equal to 42% to 44% of the fleet. Only about 5,000 TEU were scrapped in 2025. Carriers hold about USD 30bn of net cash and say they prefer a "game of chicken" to idling ships, and Maersk is ordering again (about 500,000 TEU in Q3).
  • Suez. Suez container transits rose from 54% of 2023 levels in early October to 58% to 59% by early November, and the Gemini alliance has moved services back. Clarksons estimates that a full reopening cuts TEU-mile demand by 4.8%.
  • Rates. Xeneta forecasts spot rates 30% lower in 2027, and shippers are delaying contract renewals to wait for lower rates.
  • Air. Middle Eastern carriers have restored capacity, and belly space on passenger aircraft is returning.
  • Currency. The franc took CHF 54m off EBIT in 2025, and the market regime is risk-off.

Inference. The operating environment is at or near its most favourable point, and it will deteriorate in a predictable order: DSV stabilises first (now to mid-2027), Suez routing and port congestion normalise through 2027, and the delivery wave peaks in 2028. Underneath, the structural base rate is unchanged. Trade grows at about the rate of GDP, and forwarders' unit gross profit has fallen in every period of abundant ship capacity (Sea gross profit per TEU fell 30% in 2023 and 28% year on year in Q1 2024). Unit gross profit held only in demand slowdowns without a supply wave, as in 2019.

So what. Kuehne + Nagel's volumes can keep growing at or above the market (3% to 5% a year) and still fail to protect earnings, because the external contribution to EBIT growth turns negative in 2027 through price. Richard should separate volume from yield in every quarterly report.
Strongest counter-case. Port congestion may be imposing the capacity discipline that the carriers themselves will not. Schedule reliability was 49.9% in August, with more than 4.3m TEU tied up. Maersk argues that terminal bottlenecks anchor rates, DNB Carnegie's scenario of a Red Sea delay to mid-2028 is worth up to 44% on carrier rates, and Bernstein's regression finds no meaningful relationship between freight rates and forwarders' unit gross profit over a cycle. If congestion persists and complexity stays high, 2027 yields hold and the bull case becomes the base case.
What would change my view. Suez transits stalling below 60% of 2023 levels into Q2 2027; schedule reliability still below 60% in spring 2027; Asia-Europe contract rates settling less than 10% below 2026 levels.
Market versus me. The sell-side describes every one of these headwinds in words (Morgan Stanley since September, Deutsche Bank, and Bernstein's carrier analysts), yet its numbers still have gross profit growing about 6% in 2027. The forwarder analysts stop at 2027, and the carrier analysts own 2028. I agree with the market on the direction of every force; I disagree that the forces are in the estimates.

Score: 34, set by the Rater. The 2026 lift came from forces that are reversing on a schedule: DSV's integration distraction (its recapture is planned over three to four quarters), Red Sea and Hormuz diversions holding yields up (Suez transits already at 58-59% of 2023), tariff front-loading, and a container delivery wave of 3.1m TEU in 2027 and 4.4m in 2028 against demand of about 4%. Those take unit gross profit down 4-5% a year, while lasting positives (customs complexity, technology and cloud demand, volume at or above the market) are smaller. Consensus sales growth at the 21st percentile and 3-year growth at the 4th agree. This is a scarcity price unwinding, but it hits a forwarder's yield, not a carrier's whole earnings, so the company sits well above Maersk; I am coherent with the group's 33.

#2 Internally driven corporate change forces

Conclusion: Kuehne + Nagel's internal change is strong, credible and well resourced, but it is narrow in source, gross rather than net, and already in the price, so it protects earnings rather than growing them.
Evidence, positive: the self-help is real and ahead of plan.
  • The CHF 200m structural cost programme (staff CHF 150m, facilities 30m, other 20m) delivered CHF 30m in Q1 2026 and CHF 50m in H1. It will exceed CHF 150m gross in 2026 against an opening target of CHF 100m, with the full run-rate by year-end.
  • The AI target is CHF 100m to 150m of annualised EBIT by end-2027, a 5% productivity gain on more than 25,000 white-collar staff costing CHF 1.7bn. It is built on owned platforms (SeaLOG, AirLOG and a cloud transport-management system) that only three large forwarders possess, while DSV faces a transition from CargoWise to TANGO lasting more than six years. The eTouch automation tool has already lifted Air conversion by 370 basis points and saved 1.8m staff hours.
  • The commercial machine is repaired. Small and medium-sized customers provide 52% of Sea volume, 700 dedicated sales staff hunt new accounts, and the anchor wins are Amazon and AWS, BYD, CATL and Google.
  • The organisation is leaner. The regional management layer was abolished in 2024, a Chief AI and Innovation Officer was appointed, and Road has a new head from DSV, the benchmark competitor (DSV's road margin is 4.8% against Kuehne + Nagel's about 2.6%).
  • Ownership is settled. Klaus-Michael Kühne died on 23-Aug-26, and his 53% to 56% stake passes to the Kühne Foundation, which removes the risk of a block sale or an estate sale.
Evidence, negative: the savings are gross, and capital allocation is weak.
  • Costs still rise. Headcount rose 9.0% to 92,542 (about 4,000 Contract Logistics hires in Q3), and underlying Q3 operating costs rose about 6% while the programme was saving about CHF 50m a quarter. The CFO calls the AI figure "a gross ambition rather than net EBIT", and management concedes that early gains "will likely be competed away".
  • Working capital is above target. Net working capital is 5.8% of turnover against a 4.5% to 5.5% corridor (a CHF 281m core outflow in Q3).
  • The Amazon agreement is a price concession in equity form. Kuehne + Nagel paid CHF 160m for an instrument amortised against net turnover (CHF 17m in Q3, so possibly about CHF 68m a year), sold CHF 292m of treasury shares to the hedging bank (about 1.3m shares, about 1% dilution), and has not disclosed the strike price.
  • Capital allocation is dividend-only. The CFO says buybacks are "not close to the board's heart". 2025 acquisitions of CHF 1,462m bought the Apex minority at a valuation of about CHF 3.6bn and 51% of IMC, and the put liabilities are CHF 711m.
  • Talent. Industry experts report a loss of middle-management talent after the delayering, and there is no CFO successor.

Inference. Kuehne + Nagel's self-help is a narrow, well-resourced and gross story that has been largely delivered and is already recognised by the market. It adds perhaps CHF 150m to 250m of gross EBIT capacity in 2027 against the 2026 run-rate, and a 5% fall in group gross profit (about CHF 450m) would absorb all of it. The genuinely durable internal advantage is the owned technology, which shows up as faster deployment and share gains against the long tail of smaller forwarders rather than as margin.

So what. Give management full credit for cost delivery and none for capital allocation. Model the AI benefit at 60% retention in 2027, falling to 40% by 2030, and treat the part that leaks away as lower unit gross profit, which is where it will appear.
Strongest counter-case. C.H. Robinson has shown white-collar productivity gains of 60% to 65% since 2022, and DHL 40% on booking. If Kuehne + Nagel keeps even half of a CHF 150m run-rate while DSV is still migrating systems, that is CHF 75m (5%) of EBIT that consensus does not have, and the 35% Sea and Air conversion target (32% in Q3) becomes a reason to raise estimates rather than to reset them.
What would change my view. Constant-currency operating cost growth below 2% in H1 2027 with volumes up 4% or more; a published orders-per-employee metric rising 5% or more; the Amazon charge disclosed and small.
Market versus me. Every broker has the gross savings figures, and no broker models how much of them is retained. The flat 17.2% consensus conversion rate for 2027 implicitly assumes that the savings are fully absorbed, which agrees with my view on costs. The disagreement with the market is not in this section.

Score: 63, set by the Rater. The CHF 200m programme will beat its target (over CHF 150m gross in 2026 against an opening CHF 100m), and there is a funded AI target of CHF 100-150m on owned platforms that only three forwarders have, a repaired sales engine (Amazon/AWS, BYD, CATL, Google), a new head of Road from DSV and settled Foundation ownership. Against this, the savings are gross and largely absorbed (headcount +9%, underlying costs +6%), the Amazon deal is a price concession with dilution, capital allocation is dividend-only after an expensive Apex buy-in, and middle management is being lost. A delivered, well-resourced repair that holds EBIT flat rather than growing it is a clear but partial positive, above Richard's 'gently positive but mediocre' CVS at 55 and in line with the group's 62.

#3 Industry structure, business model, financial profile and management

Conclusion: Kuehne + Nagel holds a favourable position in an unfavourable value chain, with a medium moat but no pricing power, a top-quartile financial profile with bottom-half growth, and a capable operating management whose ambition and capital allocation are conventional.

Industry and value chain. Kuehne + Nagel occupies the best stage of a poor value chain. It is joint number one or two in sea freight (4.3m TEU, about 2.4% of global container volume) and in air freight (about 2.0m tonnes, level with the enlarged DSV). The top five forwarders hold well under 30% of the market, and an oligopoly exists only in large multinational tenders, where three firms compete for every account. Forwarders control about half of liner volume, own no ships, subcontract all ocean capacity and 75% to 85% of road capacity, and earn a ROCE of about 50%.

Barriers to the top tier are high: digital forwarders failed, forwarders are punishing Maersk's integrator model by diverting cargo away from it, and Amazon is a threat mainly in the US. Market share consolidates slowly towards scale and towards whoever can fund technology, which favours the top three against the long tail. DSV has the cost advantage (Air and Sea conversion of 46% against Kuehne + Nagel's 32%); Kuehne + Nagel has the advantage in owned technology and industry verticals.

Business model and moat. Kuehne + Nagel's moat is of medium strength and shows up as market share and returns on capital, not as rising unit margins. It rests on scale in buying capacity (at its limit, according to industry experts), owned technology (an advantage that should widen for two years) and switching costs in regulated verticals (pharmaceutical Cool Corridors, aerospace, semiconductors); there are almost no switching costs in transactional freight. There is no demonstrable pricing power:

  • Sea gross profit per TEU fell 9% year on year in Q2 2026 while Kuehne + Nagel was winning share.
  • A former DSV account director reports that Kuehne + Nagel priced 6% to 12% below DSV in several large tenders.
  • The Amazon structure gives away equity economics in exchange for volume.
  • Gross margins of 32% to 38% of turnover are an artefact of passing transport costs through, not a sign of pricing power.

Financial profile. Kuehne + Nagel is above average on quality and average on growth. ROIC is about 16% including goodwill, return on equity exceeds 40% because high payouts keep equity small, free cash flow conversion is about 90% to 100% through the cycle, and capital spending is about 1% of turnover. Net debt excluding leases is about CHF 0.5bn (1.43x EBITDA including CHF 2.5bn of leases), and the payout ratio is 80%. Growth is the weakness. EPS compounded at under 2% a year from 2019 to 2025 (CHF 6.65 to 7.42), around a disruption spike to CHF 22.06; consensus growth after 2026 is 5% to 6%; and the business distributes most of its cash because it cannot reinvest it at high returns (Bernstein: it "has struggled to deploy major capital at high RONIC organically").

Management. Chief Executive Stefan Paul is a proven operator who made one costly misjudgement and repaired it. He took Road from a CHF 16m loss to a 10.9% conversion rate, delivered the cost programme early and raised guidance three times; his early-2024 cuts "impaired the commercial muscle" and cost two years of volume. The CFO has been in post since 2014. Ambition is deliberately moderate: management cut the 2030 Sea and Air conversion target from 40% to about 35% in March 2025 (alongside volume growth at 1.5 times GDP), admitting that its assumptions had been "far too optimistic", while DSV targets 55%. Incentives carry no return hurdle, and pay is modest (CHF 3.2m against a peer median of about CHF 8m). The Foundation owner entrenches a dividend-first posture with no large acquisitions.

Inference and so what. Kuehne + Nagel is a high-return, cash-distributing, capably run business in the most attractive stage of a cyclical chain, without pricing power and with a modest growth engine. That profile earns a stable through-cycle multiple of about 17x EV/EBIT, the five-year average. It does not by itself justify the current 18x to 20x unless the market sees today's earnings as a trough, and they are not a trough.

Strongest counter-case. The mix of small and medium-sized customers, the vertical specialisms and permanent supply-chain complexity may make the 2026 unit gross profit (Sea about CHF 452 per TEU, about 40% above 2019) the new normal rather than a premium to be unwound. On that reading the 35% conversion target is conservative, and the business deserves a quality premium to DSV.
What would change my view. Unit gross profit holding through the 2027 contract season; a stated change in capital returns (buybacks) under the Foundation; a return hurdle in management incentives.
Market versus me. The market pays a large premium to DSV (table above) for exactly this quality and execution. I agree on the quality; I disagree that quality without pricing power or reinvestment deserves a growth multiple.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. The company is joint number one or two in sea and air and sits in the best, asset-light stage of a poor and fragmented value chain, protected by high barriers to the top tier, owned technology and some vertical switching costs. But it has a medium moat with no pricing power (it priced 6-12% below DSV in tenders), unit margins set outside the company, and a capable but conventional management with moderate targets. The figures (ROIC 18%, 88th percentile; ROE 93rd) are real, but growth is poor: EPS grew under 2% a year from 2019 to 2025, the business cannot reinvest at high returns, the Apex minority was bought at about CHF 3.6bn, and earnings swing hard with the cycle. So it is above Indutrade and below Linea Directa's structural cost advantage, coherent with the four groups (54, 54, 64, 53).

#4 Guidance conservatism, sell-side management and the track record

Conclusion: Kuehne + Nagel's guidance is credible and conservative for the current year, with a strong recent record of beats and raises, but its method is untested in a falling-yield year and the record in such years is one of misses, so positive guidance news in H1 2027 is not evidence against the plateau.

Evidence: the current year is effectively settled. FY2026 recurring EBIT guidance is CHF 1.5bn to 1.6bn, raised in April, July and October from an opening midpoint of about CHF 1.3bn. Nine-month EBIT is CHF 1,124m, so the range implies a Q4 of CHF 376m to 476m, against CHF 435m in Q3 2026 and about 351m in Q4 2025. The base case has CHF 430m for Q4 and consensus about 424m, which gives about an 80% probability that FY2026 lands inside the range and 55% that it lands in the upper half. Each of the last four quarters beat consensus by 7% to 14%; in Q3 2026, for example, EBIT of CHF 435m beat consensus of 398m by 9%.

Evidence: the method is new. Kuehne + Nagel has given quantitative guidance only since March 2025. Management cut its first range (FY2025, CHF 1.5bn to 1.75bn) twice, to "above CHF 1.3bn", then beat it at 1.38bn, and afterwards adopted the beatable corridor that Deutsche Bank's analyst had asked for. Guidance is specific on costs (the cost programme by type and year, and the AI baseline) and silent on volumes and unit gross profit, the variables that drive the variance of results. Management's informal commentary runs ahead of consensus for 2027: AI "will become our competitive moat", and consolidation has "structurally increased pricing power". In comparable falling-yield years the record is poor: Q4 2023 EBIT missed consensus by 24%, and FY2019 missed by 4% and brought a 33% dividend cut.

Inference. Kuehne + Nagel's current guidance is mildly conservative and credible, but its "sandbagging precision" has been observed only in a rising market. The single most important scheduled event is 2-Mar-27, when the first FY2027 range is set: I put 65% on a midpoint at or below CHF 1.55bn, below consensus of CHF 1,644m. A low starting range makes a raise at the Q1 or Q2 2027 results more likely than not; the risk then moves to the Q3 2027 results and to the FY2028 range in March 2028. The timeline below gives the probability of each step.

So what. Guidance news and the fundamental path will diverge in 2027: two quarters that look like 2026, then the turn. Richard should treat the FY2028 range, not the 2027 raises, as the test of the plateau thesis, and should expect the shares to react to the March 2027 range even though that range will be consistent with Viewforth's base case.
Strongest counter-case. Management, rewarded three times for raising guidance, may set the FY2027 range near consensus to avoid a de-rating and then deliver H1 on the cost run-rate and the buy-sell lag. In that case consensus holds, the H1 beats are smaller, and the first negative event moves to October 2027.
What would change my view. A FY2027 range with a midpoint above CHF 1.6bn and stated yield assumptions; a quantified net (not gross) AI figure.
Market versus me. Deutsche Bank notes that "conservative in-year setups allow for regular beat-and-raise cycles", and most of the market reads each raise as confirmation of the thesis. I read the raises as a guidance method, and I take the company's record in down-cycles as the better guide to 2027-2028.

Score: 56, set by the Rater. The record is short and split. The FY2025 range (CHF 1.5-1.75bn) was cut twice to 'above 1.3bn' inside the last two years. Since then there have been four beats of 7-14% and three FY2026 raises (midpoint up about 20%), and the current guide is mildly conservative and specific on costs but silent on yields. The method has not been tested in a falling-yield year, where the record is one of misses (Q4 2023 -24%; FY2019 with a dividend cut). This is the level's 'beats since a recent rebasing, one large miss inside two years', a little better than Hexatronic's 50-52 because the 2026 delivery was strong. The sell-side group (36) shows estimates sitting above what the guide will carry.

#5 Pricing power, operating and financial leverage, cost scope and feedback loops

Conclusion: Kuehne + Nagel has very high operating leverage to price, little to volume, negligible financial leverage and real but gross cost scope, so revenue growth does not produce outsized profit growth; price does, and price is scheduled to fall before it recovers.

Evidence: costs follow shipments, not prices. Kuehne + Nagel's operating costs are about CHF 7.5bn (gross profit less EBIT). Personnel are about 70% of the total (CHF 5,148m), followed by right-of-use depreciation (CHF 658m), facilities (CHF 473m) and administration (CHF 453m). These costs follow shipment counts with an elasticity of about 0.5 and a lag of two to four quarters, and they do not follow price at all. Two very different leverages follow from that:

  • Leverage to volume is modest. In the 2009 volume collapse the best forwarders lost only about 3 points of conversion, and incremental conversion on new gross profit from volume is about 28% to 54%.
  • Leverage to unit gross profit is very high. In Q3 2026 gross profit rose 13.3% and EBIT 52.6%; in Q1 2024 Sea gross profit per TEU fell 28% and group EBIT about 40%. On the FY2026 base, each 1% of Sea and Air unit gross profit is worth about CHF 38m of EBIT (2.4%).
  • Financial leverage is negligible. Net interest is about CHF 35m to 40m (2% to 3% of EBIT), and bonds carry coupons of 0.7% to 1.0%.

Evidence: cost scope. The cost base is unusually cuttable for a services company: white-collar processing can shrink by 10% to 20% over three to five years, and more than 2,000 full-time positions have already gone. The 2024 lesson, however, is that cuts which touch customer-facing staff cost market share. Kuehne + Nagel's pricing gains are nominal and driven by mix, not real (#3).

Feedback loops. Seven feedback loops are at work, and the balancing loops that pull EBIT down dominate from mid-2027. The table sets out each loop, its effect and its timing.

Inference. At Kuehne + Nagel, price growth, not revenue growth, produces outsized profit growth, and over 2027-2028 the price lever points down while the cost lever has already been pulled. The same leverage that turned +13.3% gross profit into +52.6% EBIT in Q3 2026 turns into EBIT falls of 10% to 13% in the H2 2027 quarters of the base case. From 2029 the loops reverse again, and EBIT grows 6% to 8% a year on gross profit growth of 2% to 3%.

So what. Model EBIT as volume times unit gross profit by segment, less a semi-variable cost base; never add gross savings to consensus; and expect headlines about "strong cash conversion" in 2027 alongside EBIT downgrades.
Strongest counter-case. The buy-sell lag is positive at first in a falling market, because buy rates fall before sell rates. DSV is pruning accounts rather than attacking on price in Sea (it wants gross profit per TEU back to DKK 4.5k from 3.8k), and DHL's data show only a weak negative correlation between ocean rates and unit gross profit. On that reading, operating leverage works for Kuehne + Nagel through H1 2027 and the H2 give-back is small.
What would change my view. Segment EBIT moving less than 1.5 times the move in unit gross profit through two quarters of falling rates; a Road margin above 3.5% by 2027, which would mean the new Road management is out-executing DSV's recapture.
Market versus me. The market understands the leverage on the way up (it paid for it in 2026), and its models hold conversion flat on rising gross profit for 2027. I hold conversion roughly flat on flat gross profit, and that difference is where the EBIT gap to consensus comes from.

Score: 52, set by the Rater. Personnel are about 70% of a CHF 7.5bn cost base whose costs follow shipment counts at an elasticity of about 0.5 with a lag, so there is real operating gearing, proven both ways (Q3 2026: gross profit +13.3%, EBIT +52.6%; Q1 2024: Sea unit gross profit -28%, EBIT -40%). But that gearing runs to an externally set yield, not to pricing power the company holds; incremental conversion on volume is only 28-54% of new gross profit. Financial leverage is negligible (interest 2-3% of EBIT), cost-out scope is real but gross and partly competed away, and the balancing loops dominate 2027-2028. This is the level's 'pricing power proven only in a scarcity cycle', like Indus Holding's 52 on an external price.

#6 Forecast financials

Conclusion: the forecasts describe a three-year earnings plateau at about CHF 1.5bn of EBIT and about CHF 9 of EPS, 8% to 17% below consensus with the gap widening, followed by growth of 6% to 8% a year from 2029; there is no scope for double-digit growth, or for margins above the 2024 level, in the next four years.

The base case, and consensus.

Conversion of gross profit into EBIT is the measure to watch. The falls in net turnover reflect deflation in freight rates and surcharges and carry little meaning for profit; for the same reason the EBITDA margin on turnover rises mechanically and should not be read as an improvement.

The drivers. Volume keeps growing in the base case, but Sea and Air unit gross profit falls in 2027 and 2028, and only cost savings and Contract Logistics hold EBIT flat. In reported francs, Sea gross profit per TEU falls to about CHF 400 to 425 in 2027-2028, still 25% to 30% above 2019's CHF 317. Depreciation and amortisation of CHF 975m in 2027 compares with consensus of 928m: the Contract Logistics ramp-up suggests that consensus is about CHF 50m light on this line, worth 3% of EBIT on its own.

The bridge from FY2026 to FY2027. FY2027 EBIT ends slightly below FY2026 by construction, and the same pattern repeats in 2028. Volume growth pays for cost inflation, self-help pays for lower unit gross profit, and currency costs about CHF 35m net. The chart sets out each step.

The shape inside 2027. Quarterly EBIT keeps growing through H1 2027 and then falls. H1 2027 grows about 8% on easy comparisons, the full cost run-rate and the positive buy-sell lag. H2 2027 falls about 12% as transpacific and Asia-Europe contracts reprice and the deliveries weighted to the second half arrive. The Q3 2026 figure of CHF 435m is not exceeded until about 2029.

Scenarios for FY2027. Consensus FY2027 EBIT of CHF 1,644m sits near Viewforth's bull case. The three scenarios carry probabilities of 25%, 50% and 25%, and the range around the base case is about plus or minus 11% and symmetrical. For FY2028 the range is about CHF 1,250m to 1,760m, against consensus of 1,734m.

Growth and margins against the past. No double-digit growth is available in 2027-2028; growth of 6% to 8% a year becomes available in 2029-2030 once unit gross profit stops falling. Conversion of 16.3% to 17.7% sits above the 2025 trough of 14.1% because of CHF 300m to 350m of structural savings since 2024, but well below 2024 (19.1%) and the 2022 peak (34%). On these yields, Sea and Air conversion of about 30% in 2027-2028 and 32% in 2030 falls short of the 35% target.

The five judgements that move the value most, with the arithmetic. The base case is FY2027 EBIT of CHF 1,510m and EPS of CHF 8.94, on about 120m shares, a 25% tax rate and about CHF 30m of minority interests, so each CHF 1m of EBIT is worth about CHF 0.00625 of EPS.

  1. Sea and Air unit gross profit after the 2027 contract season. Each 1% on both is about CHF 38m of EBIT (2.4%, CHF 0.24 of EPS) before any cost response. If I am wrong by 5 points on both (Sea -9% and Air -8%, instead of -4% and -3%), EBIT falls by CHF 190m to about 1,320m (-13%), conversion to about 14.5% and EPS to about CHF 7.75; that costs about CHF 27 a share at 22.9x two-year-forward EPS, and nearer CHF 50 at a bear-market 19x. If I am wrong the other way (Sea +1%, Air +2%), EBIT is about CHF 1,700m and EPS about CHF 10.10, above consensus. Each 5-point swing is worth about CHF 1.20 of EPS.
  2. Net retention of savings against cost growth. Base operating cost growth is about 3% at constant currency in 2027. One point more (4%) takes CHF 75m off EBIT (-5%) and CHF 0.47 off EPS; one point less adds the same. If management keeps the full AI target by 2028 (CHF 125m gross retained in full rather than 50%), EBIT gains CHF 60m (+4%) and EPS CHF 0.38, and the 35% conversion target comes back into view.
  3. Volume: DSV's recapture and technology air demand. Each point of Sea volume is about CHF 20m of gross profit and each point of Air volume about CHF 18m, of which about half reaches EBIT after volume-driven costs. If Sea grows 1% and Air 0% in 2027, instead of 3% and 5% (faster recapture by DSV plus a pause in hyperscaler demand), EBIT falls by about CHF 65m (-CHF 20m from Sea and -CHF 45m from Air, or -4%) and EPS by CHF 0.40. Losing Air's high-yield mix would add to the first judgement (the bear case's Air -8%).
  4. The franc. A 10% move in the dollar is worth about CHF 36m pre-tax, or CHF 0.23 of EPS; a franc 5% stronger against all currencies costs about 2.5% of EBIT, or about CHF 0.24 of EPS. The base case assumes translation of -2% in 2027; guidance absorbed up to 5% in 2026.
  5. The multiple once the guidance raises stop. This is the largest lever on the share price rather than on EPS (#11 and #12). Each turn of two-year-forward P/E is worth about CHF 9.8 a share (4.3%) on the EPS in the valuation window. The distance from the 22.93x guideline to the ten-year median of 20.7x is about 10% of the price, and to the 10th percentile of 17.6x about 23%.

Two small items outside the model offset each other, net about -CHF 13m, which is inside the rounding of a CHF 1.5bn forecast; I change no forecast input (details in the end notes).

Market versus me. Consensus FY2027 gross profit growth of about 6% (three brokers) requires a strength Kuehne + Nagel has never shown: holding unit gross profit through a period of abundant capacity. Even Bernstein, the most positive covering house, has gross profit growing only 2.6% and gets its higher EBIT from a 17.8% conversion rate, which is a view on costs. The fourteen brokers' FY2027 EPS estimates (CHF 8.69 to 10.16) span only about 8% either side of the median, for a business whose forecasts two years out have missed by 40% to 80% at the last two turns: the brokers are clustered, not confident. Morgan Stanley (flat 2027 EBIT) and the two restricted Sell ratings are near my numbers; Jefferies and Oddo (CHF 10.16) hold the median up.

Score: 31, set by the Rater. Nil to 5% gives D. The growth is organic and there is no buyback, but it is the level's late-recovery shape: EPS falls to 8.86 by FY2028, regains the FY2026 level only in FY2029, and conversion (16.3-17.7%) stays below 2024's 19.1% and far below the 2022 peak. So I place it in the lower half of the band, though above the floor because margins sit above the 2025 trough on CHF 300-350m of structural savings.

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

Conclusion: guidance is likely to be raised once or twice in H1 2027 while estimates are cut in two steps around it, so the upgrade scope over the next 6 to 12 months is positive in form and negative in substance, and the first negative step is dated to 2-Mar-27.

Evidence and inference. Guidance, estimates and the narrative point in different directions, and the sequence matters more than the net effect.

  • Guidance. As #4 sets out, the single most likely sequence (about 45%) is a low FY2027 range in March followed by a raise in April or July 2027.
  • Estimates: the first move is down. If the range is set below consensus (65% probability), FY2027 consensus EBIT falls 4% to 7% in the weeks after 2-Mar-27, and net revision breadth turns negative for the first time since early 2026. The H1 beats then lift FY2027 estimates by 1% to 3% between April and July. The October 2027 results against the CHF 435m Q3 2026 base, and a flat FY2028 range in March 2028, then cut FY2027 estimates by a further 3% to 5% and FY2028 estimates by 5% to 8%. By March 2028 I expect FY2027 consensus EPS of about CHF 9.0 to 9.2 (6% to 8% below today) and FY2028 consensus EPS of about CHF 9.0 to 9.3 (10% to 14% below today). The probability that FY2027 consensus EPS is higher in March 2028 than today is about 20% to 25%, which is the probability of the bull case.
  • Narrative. The window for a "the sceptics were wrong again" story is April to July 2027, when beats, a raise, strong cash conversion and a maintained dividend coincide. No forwarder analyst has yet described the 2028 delivery peak, so it cannot be in the price, and its first appearance, probably alongside the FY2028 range, will meet no cushion.

Early signals before Kuehne + Nagel reports. The read-across events in the #4 timeline (DSV's Q4 in early February, Maersk's Q4 on 11-Feb-27, the Asia-Europe tender season from January to April, and the hyperscalers' capital-spending guidance in late January and late April) will signal the direction of estimates before the company's own range. Morgan Stanley's Suez transit tracker, read against the 75% threshold, is the running gauge in between.

So what. The scope for guidance upgrades is real, but the scope for estimate upgrades is limited to a brief interlude; for a stock whose multiple is supported by revisions, that is a negative dressed as a positive. In practice, H1 2027 is the window in which the shares are most likely to be strong on the company's own news, and the Q2 2027 unit gross profit figure (late July) is the first reading that says anything about H2.
Strongest counter-case. In the bull case (25%), Sea gross profit per TEU holds above CHF 440 through Q2 2027, FY2027 EBIT runs at about CHF 1.68bn, above today's consensus, and FY2027 consensus rises 2% to 4% through 2027, with FY2028 following. There is a further, overlapping probability of about 10% that management sets the range near consensus and delivers H1. Even then, relative momentum still rotates towards DSV, whose consensus was cut through 2026 and is positioned to rise on synergies and recapture.
What would change my view. A FY2027 range near or above consensus, with yield assumptions; reported Q1 2027 Sea gross profit per TEU above CHF 440; DSV's Q4 volumes still falling.
Market versus me. The market treats the beat-and-raise pattern as the expected path. The sell-side's own words (five Sell ratings, a mean rating of Hold and a median target below the price) say that it does not believe its own numbers for 2027. I side with the sell-side's words against its estimates.

Score: 24, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, is likely raised in-year (about 45% in H1 2027), but from a FY2027 range likely set below consensus on 2-Mar-27 (65%), so the de facto guide steps down against market expectations. Consensus FY2027 EPS, which sits near the bull case, is expected to be cut in two steps, ending about 6-8% lower by March 2028 and probably 4-7% lower within twelve months, against underlying growth of about 2-3%: a ratio of about -2, deep in the bottom of the Universe illustration. The narrative brightens from April to July 2027 and then turns. 3- and 6-month revisions at the 83rd-86th percentile are momentum already taken, not scope. This is coherent with the fourth-set group at 28 and slightly below Indutrade's 'downgrades as likely as upgrades', because here downgrades are the base case.

#8 Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, technicals, and peers

Conclusion: momentum is strong on every current measure and already mature on every leading indicator; because the stock has decoupled from its sector, the multiple now rests on a beat-and-raise cycle with a dated end, while DSV, the closest peer, sits at the opposite extreme.

Evidence. Kuehne + Nagel's momentum is strong on guidance (three raises in 2026), on sell-side estimates (rated A on the dashboard) and on the share price (rated B), while valuation is rated F. The table and key figures set out the measures.

Evidence: co-movement. The shares now move largely on their own news. Only 21% of their six-month movement is explained by the eighteen-stock logistics basket (R-squared; 47% in September 2025), and their beta is 0.81. The only meaningful peer link is DHL (correlation 0.52), which carries the same three dashboard letters (B, A, F) and the same twelve-month return (+54%); DSV's correlation is 0.31.

Peers. DHL is the twin "forwarder delivering" trade: its Global Forwarding conversion is above 20% for the first time in years. DSV is the mirror image: its consensus was cut through 2026, it has DKK 9bn of synergies and a restarted buyback ahead, and it trades at a 33% EV/EBIT discount to Kuehne + Nagel and about eight turns of P/E below it on 2028 earnings. The carriers, Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd, sit at the top of their valuation ranges on a rate-driven year that their own brokers expect to reverse in 2027 (Morgan Stanley expects Maersk's EBITDA to halve).

Inference. Momentum is strong in every measured dimension and at the end of its cycle in every dimension that can be dated. The strong composite reading masks deterioration in its components: target prices rising twice as fast as EPS embed an expanding multiple, sales revisions include the pass-through of fuel costs and freight rates, and the Buy share fell while estimates rose. Because the shares have decoupled from the sector, the re-rating was earned by company-specific news (three raises, beats of 7% to 14%, share gains) and is exposed to a company-specific reversal when that news stops; it also offers less protection in a sector sell-off than the 2025 correlation implied. The sector's revision cycle is set to rotate from the 2026 winners (Kuehne + Nagel, DHL and the carriers) to DSV.

So what. Momentum argues against standing in front of the shares before the H1 2027 results, and equally against buying on momentum alone: a position taken now is a position in the last two quarters of a company-specific re-rating with a known calendar for its reversal.
Strongest counter-case. Momentum of this kind persists as long as beats continue, and the base case itself says beats continue through July 2027. DSV's integration could also stumble again (its IT migration carries risk through 2028), prolonging Kuehne + Nagel's share windfall and the relative trade.
What would change my view. Revision breadth staying positive through March 2027; the Buy share rising with estimates; DSV's Q4 2026 volumes still falling.
Market versus me. The dashboard letters (A, B, F) and the share price say the market is still invested in the story; the sell-side's ratings and targets say it is not. I give more weight to the ratings and targets.

Score: 88, set by the Rater. Both measures are in the top fifth, with guidance raised three times, FY2027 EPS up 6% and 12% over three and six months, target prices up 20%, and the price at its 52-week high and 22% above a rising 200-day average. That would be A, but one part is negative: only 17% of analysts rate it a Buy (11th percentile, down 2 points while estimates rose), and the median target is 7% below the price. DSV, the closest operational peer, is the mirror image, though peers alone do not pull the letter. So I give B at the top of the band.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the case

Conclusion: the case is simple and trackable, and its fundamental risk is moderate (asset-light, low leverage, flexible costs, strong cash), but its price risk is high, because the one driver is external and contested in size, and it will be tested while the multiple sits at the 83rd to 90th percentile of its history.

Simplicity. The case is unusually simple to state and to monitor. It has one driver (Sea and Air unit gross profit) and two company indicators disclosed every quarter (gross profit per TEU and per 100kg, with volumes, unit costs and conversion). Four external gauges are published weekly or monthly (Suez transits, the Shanghai container index, Xeneta's contract indices and schedule reliability), and the calendar is dated (2-Mar-27, late April, late July and late October 2027, March 2028). The path from company statements to EPS is clean on costs and almost mechanical below EBIT: EPS is roughly (EBIT less 40) times 0.75, less 30, divided by 120. Three decision thresholds matter:

  • Sea gross profit per TEU above about CHF 440 through Q2 2027 supports consensus; below CHF 400 in any 2027 quarter confirms the bear case (Jefferies uses the same line).
  • Air gross profit per 100kg below CHF 78 is a warning.
  • Constant-currency cost growth above 3% is a warning.

Fragilities and assumptions. The whole forecast rests on one mechanism, and the final link in that mechanism is contested. Bernstein finds no meaningful relationship between freight rates and forwarders' unit gross profit over a cycle; Jefferies finds a clear one with a six-month lag, with sea yields explaining 30% to 42% of changes in Air and Sea EBIT. The 2016 episode turns out to have been a rate spike after the Hanjin bankruptcy, not a period of abundant capacity, which leaves 2023-2024 (the unwinding of a far larger premium) as the clean precedent. The other fragilities are:

  • the hyperscaler share of Air, which management will not quantify (6 to 7 points of Q3's 10% Air volume growth were share gains in these niches);
  • the lumpiness of the Amazon charge (CHF 17m a quarter is 4% of EBIT);
  • possible restructuring charges from the automation programme, which would open a gap between reported and recurring EBIT (FY2025's gap was CHF 138m, and the dividend follows reported EPS);
  • the franc;
  • a CHF 161m supplier-finance figure that is not confirmed in the filings.

Suddenness and prevalence. The most likely sudden risk, a fast Suez normalisation, is also the largest, and it is correlated with the second, a tariff shock on China trade. Sentiment risks are common and need no fundamental cause: a rotation into DSV on its Q4 results, a narrative of collapsing carrier earnings, a de-rating on the idea that AI commoditises intermediaries, or the risk-off regime unwinding the strongest chart in the group. Short interest reached 7% to 8% in early 2024 and about 12% in 2023, so the stock attracts cyclical short sellers.

Materiality to the price, and precedent. In each of the last three cycles the multiple de-rated by a quarter to a third before or with the first earnings cut, and forecasts two to three years out missed by 40% to 80% at the last two turns; today's dispersion of plus or minus 8% among brokers is narrower than that record warrants.

A fair trough is about CHF 145 to 175, 26% to 39% below today: that is 17.6x on EPS 15% below consensus, and the 52-week low and the Jefferies and Morgan Stanley bear values cluster at CHF 143 to 164. A severe case (16.6x on EPS back near CHF 7.4) is about CHF 120 to 125. The downside to the fair trough is one and a half to two times the upside to the highest broker target (CHF 280).

Sector and cyclicality. Forwarders are late-cycle beneficiaries of scarce carrier capacity and give the benefit back when capacity becomes abundant; the 2027-2028 supply wave is the largest on record, leaving the fleet 63% larger than in 2019 by end-2027. The contested link between freight rates and unit gross profit widens the range of outcomes rather than shifting it: the bull case deserves as much respect as the bear case around the base, which is why the scenario weights stay at 25:50:25.

Market versus me. The market prices the simple, demonstrated parts of the case (cost delivery and cash) and not the externally set variable, and the sell-side's narrow dispersion understates the risk. I think the fundamental risk is moderate and the price risk high, and that the two compound, because the most likely negative event arrives when the multiple is at the top of its range.

Score: 45, set by the Rater. The memo's FY2027 EPS cone is CHF 7.80-10.00 around 8.94 (about -13% to +12%). The case is simple and trackable: one driver, two quarterly KPIs, weekly external gauges and a dated calendar, and below EBIT it is mechanical with negligible leverage. But that one driver is external, cyclical and contested in size, a sudden Suez normalisation could cut ocean yields 20-30% within two quarters, and forecasts two to three years out missed by 40-80% at the last two turns. With the multiple at the 83rd-90th percentile and 26-39% to a fair trough, the price risk is high. This is the level's simple-mechanism, exogenous-input case placed below the middle, coherent with the groups' 42 and 47.

#10 Lifecycle phase

Conclusion: the stock is in the late Broadening phase, likely to pass through a brief Reinforcing pattern in H1 2027 and to begin Stalling in H2 2027, with Bottoming and Turning Up plausible in 2028-2029 rather than Collapsing.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule places the stock in the Broadening phase, and the backward-looking evidence agrees: over twelve months the thesis has widened from cost recovery to share gains, a technology and cloud growth story and the Amazon partnership; guidance has been raised three times; earnings momentum is rated A; and the multiple has re-rated from 16.6x (September 2025) to about 22x. The forward-looking evidence says the phase is in its last quarters. The Buy share is 17% and falling while estimates rise, the median target is below the price, the catalysts for reversal are dated (DSV's recovery, Suez, the delivery wave and tough H2 2027 comparisons), consensus sits near Viewforth's bull case, and the quarterly EBIT path turns negative year on year in Q3 2027.

Inference. The stock is in late Broadening, on the edge of Reinforcing: one or two more beats and a raise in H1 2027 would complete the Reinforcing pattern. Stalling is dated to H2 2027, when the first miss against the CHF 435m Q3 2026 base lands and the FY2028 range disappoints. The phases after that are the interesting ones: Bottoming in 2028, as the delivery wave peaks and the multiple reaches its median or below, then Turning Up into 2029-2030, when EBIT growth of 6% to 8% a year becomes visible.

So what. None of Richard's target setups is available today (#13), but the stock is a strong candidate for the "quality cyclical at trough-on-trough" setup in 2028, when the multiple is likely to be at or below its 20.7x median on EPS that has stopped falling.
Strongest counter-case. If unit gross profit holds (the bull case), the stock stays in the Reinforcing phase through 2027, management raises the 35% conversion target, and the multiple stays at or above 22x; the dashboard's rule would then be right for longer than I think.
What would change my view. The Q2 2027 unit gross profit figures and the midpoint of the FY2027 range; DSV's Q4 2026 volumes.
Market versus me. The dashboard rule and the share price say Broadening; I say late Broadening with the stall scheduled. The difference is one of timing, not of kind.

Score: 42, set by the Rater. The computed Broadening is right only at its end. The thesis has widened and guidance was raised three times, but the buy share is 17% and falling, the median target is below the price, consensus sits near the bull case, and the memo dates the first year-on-year EBIT decline and miss to Q3 2027, inside twelve months. That makes it late Broadening with a brief Reinforcing pattern in H1 2027 and then Stalling. It is not Collapsing (cost floor, cash rising, covered dividend), so it sits below BP's late Reinforcing at a commodity peak and above National Grid's established Stall.

#11 The fair multiple

Conclusion: the guideline fair multiple of 22.93x is defensible for the three-year horizon but generous for the 18-month one, where the ten-year median of 20.7x is the better anchor for a stock about to stall; the gap between the two multiples is about 10% of the price.

Evidence. The guideline fair multiple for the Broadening phase is 22.93x two-year-forward P/E, the 80th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history (116 months used, four outlier months excluded). Across that history the 10th percentile is 17.6x ("crash"), the median 20.7x ("prudent"), the 75th percentile 22.5x ("defendable") and the 90th percentile 24.2x ("mania"). Today the multiple is about 21.9x to 22.2x on consensus EPS (dashboard, 6-Nov) but 24.9x on the model's EPS at CHF 227.10, because Viewforth's two-year-forward EPS is about 9% below consensus. On EV/EBIT the stock trades at about 18x to 20x against a five-year average of 16x to 17x. Among peers, DSV trades at about 15x FY2027 earnings (#3) and DHL at about 17x, in line with its ten-year median; before the pandemic, the median forward P/E of both Kuehne + Nagel and DSV was about 22x.

Inference. The 22.93x guideline is a Broadening-phase multiple, and the phase is near its end; in each of the last three stalls the multiple fell to 16.5x to 17.6x within twelve to eighteen months (#9).

  • For the 18-month horizon ending in March 2028, when the stall should be visible and the FY2028 range set, the fairer anchor is nearer the ten-year median of 20.7x; 22.93x is defensible only through mid-2027, while beats continue.
  • For the three-year horizon ending in September 2029, when the 2029-2030 recovery is in the forward window and the delivery wave has peaked, a return towards 22x is reasonable, so the guideline is a fair three-year anchor.

The quality case for a premium to DSV (higher returns, owned technology, organic execution) is real. DSV's history, however, shows the two trading at parity when both are executing well, and DSV will be executing well in 2027-2028, with synergies, buybacks and a 55% conversion target.

So what. Applying 22.93x gives Richard the return "if the market keeps paying a Broadening multiple for a stock that has stopped growing". It is the right multiple for the exercise and the generous end of the plausible range; #12 shows the return at the median and at the 10th percentile.
Strongest counter-case. Morgan Stanley's bull case puts 21x EV/EBIT on FY2027 (one standard deviation above history), arguing that complexity stays high and automation makes margins structurally higher. If the business has permanently raised its conversion floor, the ten-year percentiles understate what the market will pay, and the 80th percentile could become the new median.
What would change my view. A FY2027 range near consensus, or Sea gross profit per TEU above CHF 440 in Q1 2027, would justify holding the guideline multiple through 2027. Conversely, a Q2 2027 figure below CHF 420 would move my 18-month anchor to 20.7x or below immediately.
Market versus me. The market pays about 22x on its own EPS and about 25x on mine. I think 22.93x is the ceiling of fair value for the next 18 months, and the market's own history says that the fair multiple for a stalling forwarder is 17x to 21x.

Score: 17, set by the Rater. Dear on both gives F. The dearness is not deserved: the stock is about to stall, and on the memo's EPS the two-year-forward multiple is about 25x, above the 90th-percentile 'mania' line of 24.2x. I lift it a little inside the band because on consensus it is about 22x, only about 7% above the 20.7x ten-year median, and part of the peer gap is DSV's own trough (2nd percentile of its history) rather than this stock's premium.

  • The multiple (-7.9% in both horizons) is the move from 24.9x on the model's EPS today to 22.93x at the horizon. On consensus EPS today's multiple is about 22x, so the de-rating in the model is the market discovering Viewforth's lower EPS, not a change in what the market pays for earnings.
  • Earnings (+7.1% to March 2028) is the two-year-forward EPS moving from about CHF 9.1 today (FY2027-2028, the plateau years) to about CHF 9.8 (three-quarters FY2029 and one quarter FY2030, the recovery years). To September 2029 (+16.5%) it reaches about CHF 10.6 (FY2030-2031). The implied price is about CHF 224 in March 2028 and about CHF 244 in September 2029. The earnings part of the return therefore comes entirely from FY2029-2030, the least certain years of the forecast, while the shareholder lives through the plateau years.
  • Dividends (+6.5% and +9.6%) are CHF 7.50 for FY2026 and 7.25 for FY2027 within the 18-month window, and 7.00 for FY2028 beyond it. That is a yield of about 3.1% at today's price, covered about 1.5 times by free cash flow in 2027 (CHF 1.35bn against about CHF 900m paid), while net debt excluding leases falls to about CHF 0.3bn. If the Foundation owner holds the dividend at CHF 7.50 (about a 50% probability), the 18-month return gains roughly a point and the market would read the decision as a positive signal. There are no buybacks in the return, and I expect none.

Market versus me. The market's implied return is the consensus EPS path (+6% and +5%) at a held multiple, plus the yield: about 9% to 10% a year. Mine is 3.6% a year to March 2028 at the generous multiple, and about zero once the scenarios are weighted.

Score: 20, set by the Rater. A loss gives F, and -3% maps to about 22 on the scale. I move it down two for the fat, negatively skewed lower tail (bear -35%, downside to fair trough 1.5-2 times the upside to the highest target). I hold it off the floor because the three-year check at the guideline multiple is about +12% from today, mostly dividends plus the 2029-2030 recovery.

#13 Summary conclusion on the business and the investment case

Everything that is good about Kuehne + Nagel is already in the price; the mechanism that will set its 2027-2028 earnings is not.

Kuehne + Nagel is a high-quality operator in the best stage of a poor value chain, and it is better run than at any point since 2022. Its cost base is CHF 300m to 350m leaner than it would otherwise be, its owned technology lets it automate faster than DSV, its commercial engine is repaired, its financial leverage is negligible, its cash conversion is near 100% through a cycle, and its new owner is stable. None of that is in dispute, and all of it is in the price.

What is not in the price is the mechanism that set 2026's earnings: Sea and Air unit gross profit. That variable is set outside the company, by carrier capacity and shippers' contract behaviour; each 1% move in it changes EBIT by 2.4%; and over the next two years it faces the largest container delivery wave on record, a reopening Suez Canal and returning air capacity. Viewforth's base case therefore holds EBIT flat at about CHF 1.5bn through 2028, with EPS of about CHF 9, 8% to 17% below a consensus that extrapolates growth of 5% to 6% a year, before EBIT grows 6% to 8% a year from 2029.

The shape of the next 18 months is the most useful insight in this memo. Kuehne + Nagel guides low in March and then raises, so H1 2027 should bring beats, a raise, strong cash conversion and a maintained dividend. Around that interlude, the FY2027 range in March 2027, and the Q3 2027 results and FY2028 range from October 2027, should trigger two rounds of estimate cuts. Richard's question is where fundamental outcomes and the probability of upgrades are unusually skewed to the positive. For Kuehne + Nagel in 2027-2028 they are skewed to the negative, from a top-quintile multiple that the stock reached on its own news, with a brief positive interlude from April to July 2027. The constructive opportunity is dated too: a trough-on-trough setup in 2028, when the delivery wave peaks, the multiple is at or below its median and the 2029-2030 recovery becomes forecastable. The quarterly unit gross profit figures will show exactly when that setup arrives.

End notes

Bases and definitions. EBIT is the company's recurring EBIT, the basis of its guidance (FY2025: CHF 1,380m recurring against 1,242m reported; the gap is restructuring). Gross profit is the company's own line (net turnover less transport costs) and is the denominator of the conversion rate (EBIT divided by gross profit). Free cash flow follows the company's definition: after capital spending and lease principal, before dividends and acquisitions. Net debt excludes leases. Viewforth EPS is the Investment Analyst's cross-check figure after minority interests (CHF 9.30 for FY2026); the model's own EPS (CHF 9.46 for FY2026) is before minority interests and is the basis of the return calculation in #12. Consensus is the FactSet median at 26-Oct-26 unless a chart says otherwise.

Two small items outside the model. A review of the model flagged two items that are not in it and that offset each other. First, the CHF 4m Sea depreciation credit in Q3 2026 was a reclassification with no effect on EBIT, so the -CHF 15m depreciation step in the FY2027 bridge should not be there (+1% to FY2027 EBIT). Second, the Amazon charge at its Q3 run-rate (about CHF 68m a year) is about CHF 28m above the CHF 40m in the model (-1.8%). The net effect is about -CHF 13m, inside the rounding of a CHF 1.5bn forecast, so no forecast input changes.

Default visuals. Charts and tables marked as FactSet use FactSet's reported basis for history and the FactSet median or mean for consensus, as noted under each; Viewforth figures come from the one-page summary of the Financial Analyst's model (model update 1, run at CHF 227.10 on 26-Oct-26). The share price and valuation charts are the Master Dashboard's. The five financial tables (annual history, recent periods, FactSet consensus, broker detail and segments) are Richard's standard tables.

Visuals drawn for this memo. The supply balance, guidance record, EBIT bridge, quarterly EBIT path, FY2027 scenarios, revision path, Sea gross profit per TEU, price ladder, scenario returns, segment EBIT and de-rating precedents are drawn from the figures in the memo text. The FY2027 sensitivity grid applies the memo's own rules of thumb linearly and before any cost response or volume change, so its cells differ slightly from the memo's rounded scenario figures. The expected revision path applies the memo's percentage steps to today's FY2027 consensus EPS of CHF 9.78 and shows the resulting ranges.

Grades. A 90 to 100, B 75 to 89, C 50 to 74, D 25 to 49, F 1 to 24.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
